title: Introduction
content:
1. Overview of Amazon EC2 Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) provides virtual servers in the AWS Cloud. It allows users to deploy and manage computing resources without maintaining physical servers.
In this project, an EC2 instance named KLTN-Web-Server hosts the Nginx web server. The instance is deployed in a private subnet and receives web traffic through the Application Load Balancer (ALB).
The instance does not have a public IPv4 address. Administrative access is provided through AWS Systems Manager Session Manager.
Deployment Objectives Deploy an EC2 instance inside the project VPC.
Place the instance in a private subnet.
Attach an IAM role for Systems Manager access.
Use Session Manager for secure administration.
Install and verify the Nginx web server.
Configure Security Groups to restrict network traffic.
2. EC2 Instance Configuration Component Configuration Instance Name KLTN-Web-Server Instance Type t3.micro VPC KLTN-VPC Subnet KLTN-Private-Subnet Private IPv4 10.0.2.35 Public IPv4 Not assigned Web Server Nginx Management Method AWS Systems Manager Session Manager IAM Role KLTN-EC2-SSM-Role Reviewing the EC2 Instance To review the deployed instance:
Open the Amazon EC2 service. Select Instances. Find KLTN-Web-Server. Review its instance type, VPC, subnet, private IP address, and public IP address. Confirm that the instance is running and its status checks have passed. The instance is deployed in the private network to reduce direct exposure to the Internet.
3. Configuring IAM Role for Systems Manager AWS Systems Manager Session Manager allows administrators to access an EC2 instance without opening an inbound SSH port or managing SSH key pairs.
The project uses the IAM role KLTN-EC2-SSM-Role with the AWS-managed policy AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore.
To review the role:
Open the IAM service. Select Roles. Find KLTN-EC2-SSM-Role. Review its trusted entity and attached permissions. Confirm that the role is assigned to KLTN-Web-Server. The EC2 instance uses this role to communicate with Systems Manager.
4. Accessing the Instance Through Session Manager To establish a management session:
Open the EC2 console. Select KLTN-Web-Server. Click Connect. Select Session Manager. Start the session. The session provides terminal access without requiring a public IP address or inbound SSH access.
5. Configuring Security Groups A Security Group acts as a virtual firewall for AWS resources. It controls inbound and outbound traffic according to defined rules.
The project applies Security Groups to restrict access to the web server and supporting network components.
Component Protocol Port Purpose ALB Security Group TCP 80 Receive HTTP requests EC2 Security Group TCP 80 Allow HTTP traffic forwarded by the ALB VPC Endpoint Security Group TCP 443 Allow HTTPS communication from the EC2 instance The EC2 Security Group is configured to allow web traffic from the ALB Security Group rather than directly from arbitrary Internet sources.
No inbound SSH rule is required for administration because Session Manager is used.
6. Installing and Verifying Nginx Nginx is the web server installed on the EC2 instance.
After connecting through Session Manager, the following commands can be used on Ubuntu:
sudo apt update sudo apt install nginx -y Start and enable the service:
sudo systemctl start nginx sudo systemctl enable nginx Check the service:
sudo systemctl status nginx To verify the local web server response:
curl -I http://localhost A successful HTTP response confirms that Nginx is responding locally on the instance.
7. Verification Results The following configurations were verified during implementation:
KLTN-Web-Server is running.
The instance uses private IP address 10.0.2.35.
No public IPv4 address is assigned.
The instance has the KLTN-EC2-SSM-Role IAM role.
Session Manager can establish a terminal session.
Nginx is running and responds to local HTTP requests.
Expected Results The project has a private EC2 web server running Nginx. Session Manager provides administrative access, while Security Groups restrict network communication to the required traffic.
This configuration reduces direct exposure of the server and provides a foundation for web traffic protection through the Application Load Balancer and AWS WAF.

REPORT ON THE MINI MEETUP – FIRST CLOUD AI JOURNEY 1. Mini Meetup Objectives The Mini Meetup – First Cloud AI Journey was a knowledge-sharing event organized by the FCAJ community for people interested in Cloud, AI, and modern technologies. The event provided an opportunity for participants to gain foundational knowledge of cloud computing, explore different server infrastructure options, and learn how to build a personal brand in the technology industry.
The main objectives of the mini meetup were:
To explore fundamental concepts and learning pathways in Cloud Computing. To understand the differences between common hosting models and server options. To learn how to build a personal brand through LinkedIn to support academic and career development. To connect and exchange knowledge with a community of people who share an interest in Cloud and technology. 2. Speakers and Topics Phung Hai Long – Marketing Manager, Thanh Cong Group: LinkedIn and Personal Branding. Phuong Nguyen: The Very First Step into the Cloud. Pham Minh Quang: Right Server, Right Job – Comparing Hosting Types and Server Options. 3. Key Topics 3.1. LinkedIn and Personal Branding The first session discussed the role of LinkedIn in building a professional image and creating career opportunities. In addition to technical knowledge, presenting one’s skills, experience, and career goals clearly is also important for information technology students.
Key takeaways included:
Building a professional LinkedIn profile that clearly communicates personal interests and career objectives. Presenting technical skills, knowledge, and completed projects to demonstrate professional capabilities. Connecting with technology communities, industry professionals, and people with similar interests. Sharing learning experiences and practical projects to gradually establish professional credibility. 3.2. The Very First Step into the Cloud The second session focused on the first steps toward understanding cloud computing. This topic was directly relevant to my internship and research into AWS infrastructure security.
The key learning points included:
Understanding the concept of Cloud Computing and the benefits of accessing computing resources over the Internet. Becoming familiar with cloud service models, resource provisioning, and scalability. Recognizing the importance of foundational knowledge in networking, servers, storage, and security before deploying cloud systems. Developing an appropriate learning path that combines theoretical knowledge with hands-on practice on cloud platforms. Through this session, I recognized that computer networking is an important foundation for learning AWS services, configuring network connectivity, and designing secure cloud infrastructure.
3.3. Right Server, Right Job – Comparing Hosting Types and Server Options The third session introduced common hosting models and server options, emphasizing that infrastructure decisions should be based on the actual requirements of each system.
Key topics included:
Exploring common hosting models and server types, along with their differences. Evaluating factors such as performance, scalability, level of control, security, and operating costs. Understanding that server infrastructure should be selected according to the purpose and requirements of an application. Recognizing the importance of balancing technical requirements with budget constraints when designing infrastructure. These insights provided a useful foundation for selecting appropriate AWS resources, such as Amazon EC2, when deploying and securing cloud infrastructure.
4. Knowledge and Skills Gained 4.1. Technical Knowledge Cloud Computing: Strengthened my understanding of cloud computing and its role in delivering IT resources. Server Infrastructure: Gained a clearer perspective on selecting hosting models and server configurations according to system requirements. Computer Networking: Better understood the relationship between networking fundamentals and connectivity management in cloud environments. Security and Cost Optimization: Recognized the importance of balancing performance, security, and cost when designing IT systems. 4.2. Personal Development Skills Learned more about the role of LinkedIn in building a professional profile and expanding a professional network. Developed a clearer direction for presenting technical skills, knowledge, and practical projects. Recognized the importance of self-learning, keeping up with technological developments, and sharing knowledge with the community. 5. Application to My Internship Project My internship and research project is titled “Research and Implementation of Infrastructure Security on AWS.”
The knowledge gained from the meetup can be applied to my project in the following ways:
Infrastructure Selection: Apply knowledge of server options to select suitable AWS resources, particularly Amazon EC2, for deploying the system. Cloud Infrastructure Design: Use foundational networking knowledge to design VPCs, public and private subnets, route tables, and secure network connectivity. Infrastructure Security: Understand the importance of access control, network protection, and security configurations when deploying AWS resources. Cost Optimization: Select appropriate resource configurations, monitor resource utilization, and minimize unnecessary expenses during practical implementation. Professional Portfolio Development: Document the implementation process, technical challenges, and project outcomes to build a portfolio for future academic and career opportunities. 6. Event Experience Participating in the Mini Meetup – First Cloud AI Journey gave me an opportunity to explore different perspectives on technology and career development. The three sessions combined technical knowledge of cloud computing, server infrastructure selection, and personal branding.
Through the session The Very First Step into the Cloud, I became more motivated to strengthen my foundational knowledge and continue practicing with AWS. The discussion about hosting models and server options helped me recognize that successful system deployment involves more than simply making a service work; performance, suitability, security, and cost must also be considered.
In addition, the LinkedIn session helped me better understand the importance of building a professional profile and showcasing practical projects when developing a career in information technology.
7. Conclusion and Lessons Learned Through the Mini Meetup – First Cloud AI Journey on August 15, 2026, I gained additional insights into cloud computing, server infrastructure options, and personal branding in the technology industry.
The most important lesson was the need to combine foundational knowledge with practical experience while selecting technical solutions based on system requirements, security, and budget constraints. These insights will support my continued learning of AWS and the implementation of a more secure cloud infrastructure as part of my internship project.

title: Proposal
content:
⚠️ Note: The information below is for reference purposes only. Please do not copy verbatim for your report, including this warning.
WEB TRAVEL PLATFORM ON CLOUD High-Availability and Auto-Scaling AWS Architecture Solution for Online Tour Booking Systems 1. Executive Summary Web Travel Platform is designed and deployed to modernize online tour management, searching, and booking systems on the Amazon Web Services (AWS) cloud platform. The system operates reliably in a live cloud environment with flexible auto-scaling capabilities ranging from 0 to a maximum of 3 application servers depending on incoming traffic. The platform leverages core AWS services (VPC, EC2, RDS, Auto Scaling) to ensure high availability, strict data isolation, and operational cost optimization within the 100 USD AWS Promotional Credits budget.
2. Problem Statement What’s the Problem? Traditional web applications deployed on a single physical server or local environment (such as XAMPP) frequently experience overloading during peak tourism seasons when user traffic surges. Hosting both web source code and the database on the same server increases the risk of data breaches, complicates backup and recovery procedures, and introduces a Single Point of Failure (SPOF).
The Solution The platform utilizes Amazon VPC to segment the network infrastructure into public and private tiers across two Availability Zones. The application tier runs on Amazon EC2 (Ubuntu 24.04 LTS) hosting PHP source code, integrated with an Auto Scaling Group and a custom AMI template to automatically replicate servers when needed. The data tier is migrated to the managed Amazon RDS (MySQL) service, completely isolated inside a Private Subnet and protected by two layers of Security Groups.
Benefits and Return on Investment The solution completely eliminates upfront physical server hardware investment and maintenance costs while enhancing system reliability and customer data security. Actual operational costs are kept minimal (nearly 0 USD when stopped in standby mode and approximately 0.025 USD/hour when both EC2 and RDS are active), fitting comfortably within the 100 USD Credits academic grant. The system significantly reduces manual infrastructure administration overhead and is ready for immediate enterprise-scale expansion.
3. Solution Architecture The platform adopts a standard multi-tier AWS cloud architecture in the Singapore Region (ap-southeast-1). The entire infrastructure resides within a custom Virtual Private Cloud named travel-vpc, spanning two Availability Zones (ap-southeast-1a and ap-southeast-1b). The web server Web-travel-sv is placed inside a Public Subnet, receiving user traffic through an Internet Gateway and the TL-Web security group. Business data is queried internally from travel-database (Amazon RDS MySQL) located in a Private Subnet protected by the TL-Database security group. The Travel-auto-scaling-group, combined with Web-Travel-AMI and Travel-target, guarantees elastic scalability and continuous user session persistence.
4. Technical Implementation Implementation Phases The project was executed over 10 weeks (conducted regularly every Saturday) across four primary phases:
Survey and Source Code Standardization (Weeks 1 – 2): Tested the Web Travel application locally on XAMPP, exported the travel_test.sql database dump, and established centralized version control on GitHub (dt-kien04/du-an-01). Network and Security Setup (Weeks 3 – 4): Provisioned travel-vpc, segmented 2 Public Subnets and 2 Private Subnets, and configured the TL-Web and TL-Database security groups. Database and Web Server Deployment (Weeks 5 – 7): Launched Amazon RDS (travel-database), provisioned the Ubuntu EC2 instance (Web-travel-sv), installed the LAMP stack, cloned source code from GitHub, and established database connectivity. Auto-Scaling Configuration and Operational Optimization (Weeks 8 – 10): Packaged Web-Travel-AMI, configured the Target Group (Travel-target), Launch Template (Travel-template), and Auto Scaling Group, and finalized the graduation thesis documentation. Technical Requirements Application Tier (Web Tier): Amazon EC2 t3.micro virtual instance running Ubuntu Server 24.04 LTS, configured with Apache2, PHP 8.x, MySQL Client, and Git. Remote administrative access is authenticated via an SSH Key Pair (khoa-travel.pem). Data Tier (Database Tier): Amazon RDS running MySQL Community Edition on a db.t4g.micro instance with 20 GiB SSD (gp2) storage, public access disabled (Public access = No), and a 1-day automated backup retention period.
5. Timeline & Milestones Project Timeline Preparation Phase (Weeks 1 – 2): Studied AWS cloud fundamentals, activated the 100 Credits account, standardized PHP source code, and pushed the repository to GitHub.
8. Expected Outcomes Technical Improvements: Successfully deliver a stable, live online tour booking platform on the AWS cloud featuring a highly secure multi-tier network architecture, eliminating single points of failure and enabling seamless auto-scaling under high traffic loads.
Long-term Value Establish a standardized cloud architecture foundation ready for future enterprise upgrades, including offloading static image assets to Amazon S3 + CloudFront, integrating a custom domain via Amazon Route 53 with HTTPS (ACM) encryption, and automating deployments via CI/CD pipelines.

Secure Hybrid Access to S3 using VPC Endpoints Overview AWS PrivateLink provides private connectivity to AWS services from VPCs and your on-premises networks, without exposing your traffic to the Public Internet.
In this lab, you will learn how to create, configure, and test VPC endpoints that enable your workloads to reach AWS services without traversing the Public Internet.
You will create two types of endpoints to access Amazon S3: a Gateway VPC endpoint, and an Interface VPC endpoint. These two types of VPC endpoints offer different benefits depending on if you are accessing Amazon S3 from the cloud or your on-premises location
Gateway - Create a gateway endpoint to send traffic to Amazon S3 or DynamoDB using private IP addresses.You route traffic from your VPC to the gateway endpoint using route tables. Interface - Create an interface endpoint to send traffic to endpoint services that use a Network Load Balancer to distribute traffic. Traffic destined for the endpoint service is resolved using DNS. Content Workshop overview Prerequiste Access S3 from VPC Access S3 from On-premises VPC Endpoint Policies (Bonus) Clean up

title: Sharing and Feedback
content:
⚠️ Note: The information below is for reference purposes only. Please do not copy verbatim for your report, including this warning.
Here, you can freely share your personal opinions about your experience participating in the First Cloud AI Journey program. This will help the FCAJ team improve any shortcomings based on the following aspects:
Overall Evaluation 1. Working Environment
The working environment is very friendly and open. FCAJ members are always willing to help whenever I encounter difficulties, even outside working hours. The workspace is tidy and comfortable, helping me focus better. However, I think it would be nice to have more social gatherings or team bonding activities to strengthen relationships.
2. Support from Mentor / Team Admin
The mentor provides very detailed guidance, explains clearly when I don’t understand, and always encourages me to ask questions. The admin team supports administrative tasks, provides necessary documents, and creates favorable conditions for me to work effectively. I especially appreciate that the mentor allows me to try and solve problems myself instead of just giving the answer.
3. Relevance of Work to Academic Major
The tasks I was assigned align well with the knowledge I learned at university, while also introducing me to new areas I had never encountered before. This allowed me to both strengthen my foundational knowledge and gain practical skills.
4. Learning & Skill Development Opportunities
During the internship, I learned many new skills such as using project management tools, teamwork skills, and professional communication in a corporate environment. The mentor also shared valuable real-world experiences that helped me better plan my career path.
5. Company Culture & Team Spirit
The company culture is very positive: everyone respects each other, works seriously but still keeps things enjoyable. When there are urgent projects, everyone works together and supports one another regardless of their position. This made me feel like a real part of the team, even as an intern.
6. Internship Policies / Benefits
The company provides an internship allowance and offers flexible working hours when needed. In addition, having the opportunity to join internal training sessions is a big plus.
